questions.q: Where did specialized agriculture first appear, according to Diamond?
a: Mesopotamia, followed by China and Mesoamerica
Egypt, followed by Europe and India
Africa, followed by Australia and Asia
China, followed by Mesopotamia and Peru
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the first traces of specialized farming were found in Mesopotamia.

questions.q: What did living alongside animals bring to early farming societies?
a: More germs and disease, but eventually stronger immunity
A larger supply of meat and no illness
New tools and faster travel routes
A belief that animals were sacred
questions.why: Lesson 1 says animal proximity brought disease, and survivors passed immunity to their children.

questions.q: How did language develop in the summary's account?
a: Communities needed records as they collaborated on farming
People invented it to write down religious laws
Traders created it to keep prices secret
Rulers imposed it to control distant provinces
questions.why: Lesson 2 says agriculture created a need for record keeping, which shaped language.

questions.q: Which direction did information mostly spread in history?
a: From east to west, rarely the other way
From west to east, rarely the other way
From north to south along river valleys
From coastal cities inland to farms
questions.why: Lesson 2 says ideas historically diffused from east to west rather than the reverse.

questions.q: What does Diamond say explains differences between societies?
a: Environmental conditions, not biological differences
Differences in intelligence between populations
The influence of religion on science
The size of a society's army and navy
questions.why: Lesson 3 rejects racial explanations and points to resources, geography and environment.
